description: We are team of three high school students
summary: We developed FireSignal, an interactive dashboard that helps people explore fire activity using satellite observations from NASA’s Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS). The project addresses the challenge of turning individual satellite detections into information people can interpret. Users can select an area and date, see where hotspots were detected, compare observations from the MODIS and VIIRS instruments, and find out how a month’s activity ranks against the same month in earlier years. This matters because a map full of hotspots tells you where satellites detected activity, while the historical comparison helps you judge whether that activity was unusual for the area and time of year. Our goal is to make NASA fire data easier for students, educators, and the public to explore and understand.
details: FireSignal combines an interactive hotspot map, a calendar, charts, and historical rankings in one dashboard. Users can filter observations by date, area, or sensor, compare MODIS and VIIRS on synchronized maps, and export filtered detections as CSV or JSON. We built the data processing and API in Python and the browser interface with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. A key design choice was to group nearby detections into hexagonal grid cells and measure how many days each cell showed activity. We used Suomi-NPP VIIRS as a reference to put monthly activity from both instruments on a comparable scale. We also accounted for seasonality by comparing each month with the same month in previous years, and distinguished days with no detections from days with unavailable data. These choices help users move from inspecting a single hotspot to asking a broader question about how fire activity changes across places, sensors, and years.
